plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Coagulation Cascade, Heparin, Vitamin K & Warfarin chart from Giulio Bizzozero (1882 Virchows Archiv 90: 261–332), Paul Morawitz (1905 Ergebnisse der Physiologie 4: 307–422), Jay McLean (1916 Am. J. Physiol. 41: 250–257), Henrik Dam (1935 Nature 135: 652–653), and Karl Paul Link & Harold Campbell (1940–1941 J. Biol. Chem. 138: 21–33) shows 1) Primary haemostasis: 150,000–400,000 platelets per microlitre (~15 million per drop) form a plug; 2) Coagulation cascade: Tissue Factor (thromboplastin) + Ca²⁺ activates Prothrombin → Thrombin, cleaving soluble Fibrinogen into insoluble Fibrin mesh; 3) Heparin brakes thrombin; and 4) Vitamin K arms clotting factors in the liver while Dicoumarol/Warfarin blocks Vitamin K recycling.

teach_overlay.label: MORAWITZ (1905) 4-FACTOR COAGULATION CASCADE (THROMBOPLASTIN + CA²⁺ → PROTHROMBIN → THROMBIN → FIBRIN) & VITAMIN K VS WARFARIN CHART
teach_overlay.detail: Inked Morawitz (1905) 4-factor coagulation cascade (Thromboplastin + Ca²⁺ → Prothrombin → Thrombin → Fibrinogen to Fibrin) & Vitamin K vs Warfarin liver cycle chart on period paper
teach_overlay.scale: a single drop of your blood holds fifteen million microscopic platelet discs waiting like deflated life rafts — the instant a vessel wall rips, they inflate spiky arms in less than a second and pile into a sandbag dam before a net of fibrin steel cables locks them solid
